Figure 1: Comparison of prompt-learning pipelines: (a) CoOp (Zhou et al., 2022b), (b) BiomedCoOp (Koleilat et al., 2025), and (c) Ours. Prior methods typically treat classes independently and rely mainly on global image representations; our approach leverages class semantic structure by shaping the teacher distribution with a class graph W and distills geometry-aware supervision over both global [IMG] token and attentive patch tokens. Only prompts are learned; the encoders remain frozen.

Figure 2: Risk–coverage across four biomedical datasets. Our method yields consistently lower curves (smaller AURC) than BiomedCoOp (Koleilat et al., 2025), indicating fewer high-confidence errors at the same coverage and improved selective reliability.

Figure 5: Probability mass on disease classes (excluded GT) on Retina dataset. Each curve is a kernel density estimate over per-image quantity s(x) = ∑ c∈D pθ(y = c | x), where D are the disease classes (Normal excluded). Legends report ∑ x s(x) (Σ): total probability mass placed on disease classes across all images in the subset. Left: subset where both methods misclassify and the ground-truth class is a disease. Right: all images with normal GT.

Table 7: Robustness comparison under label noise (random label flips) in few-shot evaluation. Average accuracy (%) across 11 datasets under different numbers of random label flips (16-shot), averaged over 3 runs.

Table 6: Robustness comparison under label-noise (random label flips) in base→novel generalization. Base/Novel/HM accuracies (%) across 10 datasets with 16 shots over 3 runs. Arrows in the AVERAGE block denote (Ours − BiomedCoOp (Koleilat et al., 2025)): green ↑ = improvement; red ↓ = drop.

Table 1: Accuracy comparison on base-to-novel generalization with state-of-the-art promptlearning methods (16-shot). Average accuracy (%) over 3 runs. Best per column is in bold; second best is underlined. HM denotes the harmonic mean between base and novel. Citations are provided in the “AVERAGE over 10 DATASETS” table.

Figure 3: From biomedical text prototypes, we build a class graph W that captures semantic relations among classes. A geometry strength γ smooths the teacher distribution and supervises two distillation losses: (1) GAD operates at the global [IMG] token; (2) LGD operates at patch-token level, where c denotes the ground-truth class. Only the student prompts are updated; the encoders and W remain frozen.
Table 5: Hyperparameters per dataset and benchmark for our method. λGAD and λLGD are loss weights; γ is the geometry strength; K/P is the top-token ratio.
Table 2: Few-shot evaluation against state-of-the-art methods. Average classification accuracy (%) over 11 datasets, reported as mean±std over 3 runs. Best results for each K (shots) are in bold.

Figure 4: Wins analysis via KDE curves on the RETINA dataset. We compare BiomedCoOp and our method on challenging test samples that our method classifies correctly while BiomedCoOp is wrong (“wins”). Left: KDE of the logit margin z(y) − maxj ̸=y z(j). Right: KDE of the probability assigned to the ground-truth class’s top-k neighbors in W (here k=3). The legend in each panel also reports Σ, the sum over all win samples.
